For the SC PC cases, comparing B12B.90 and B12B.95, the addition of higher CO capture rates results in an HHV efficiency penalty of 0.5 percentage 2 points (1.5 percent relative to B12B.90).  For the PC cases, the FGD wastewater blowdown flow rate range to be treated by the spray dryer evaporator spans 55–75 gpm. The approximate performance impact of implementing the spray dryer evaporator across the six PC cases is a 0.25–0.27 percentage point (absolute) decrease in the HHV net plant efficiency. This is due primarily to the diversion of warm flue gas away from the air preheater and to the evaporator, with an additional minor impact resulting from the small auxiliary load required by the spray dryer evaporator.  Emissions of Hg, HCl, PM, NOx, and SO are all at or below the applicable federal 2 regulatory limits currently in effect for PC technology. The primary performance and environmental profile conclusions that can be drawn from the NGCC cases are:  The NGCC H-class cases have the highest net efficiency of all the technologies, both without CO capture (55.1 percent) and with CO capture (49.0 percent at a 90 percent 2 2 capture rate). The next non-NGCC case highest efficiency is the non-capture Shell IGCC case, with an efficiency of 43.0 percent.  For the NGCC cases, adding CO capture results in a HHV efficiency penalty of 6 2 percentage points (11–12 percent relative to non-capture) for both the F-frame cases and H-frame cases. o The addition of higher CO capture rates to the F-frame cases, comparing 2 B31B.90 and B31B.95, results in an HHV efficiency penalty of 0.3 percentage points (0.7 percent relative to B31B.90).
